πλᾰτᾰγ-ώνιον , τό,
A.broad petal of the poppy or anemone, so called because lovers took omens from it, laying it on the left hand, and striking it with the right, and it was a good omen if it burst with a loud crack, Theoc. 11.57 , cf. Nic. Fr. 74.43 , Poll. 9.127 ; “τῷ μηκῶνος π.”
J. AJ 3.7.6
(vulg. πλαταγῶνι) ; cf. τηλέφιλον.
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
